A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VCFLOW research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, clarified and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original cc2017 video-reconstruction results, component and ROI-partition ablations, cortical visualizations and reconstructed examples, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and adds detailed SARA/HED ablations and visualizations comparing preprocessed data with learned semantic tokens.

M1.justification: HCAM, SARA, HED and their overall objectives remain the same. The added decoder, backbone and inference descriptions explain existing components; neither these additions nor Figure 3's clarified diffusion-prior placement establish an altered procedure.

E1.justification: The experiments retain DIR/GOD image pretraining and cc2017 reconstruction across the same three subjects. Appendix A.7 newly identifies UK Biobank as the pretrained encoder's upstream data source, but presents this as backbone provenance rather than an added training experiment or evaluation population.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains fMRI-PTE-V, GLFA, GLFA* and NEURONS*, while Table 4 retains GLFA and subject-specific NEURONS. Newly cited reconstruction methods are not added to the comparisons; the new ablation rows are VCFLOW variants.

E3.justification: Tables 5–6 add controlled subject-1 configurations varying SARA losses, HED tasks and progressive learning. Existing splits, preprocessing and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. Section 4.3's explicit N-way top-1 video-classification description clarifies the already reported evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's whole-module and ROI-partition ablations, v2 tests individual SARA objectives and HED tasks, including progressive learning, in Tables 5–6. Figure 9 adds UMAP and t-SNE comparisons of inputs and semantic tokens across subjects. These substantially deepen examination of the central components and subject alignment.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging frame-classification accuracy over 100 trials and provide per-subject and averaged point estimates. v2 adds no training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the original reconstruction examples retain their results. New diagnostic results include subject-1 frame 50-way accuracy of 7.52% with only SARA's alignment loss versus 14.2% with all SARA losses, and 11.3% without HED progressive learning versus 14.2% with it. Figure 9 adds qualitative subject-distribution evidence; these are supplementary findings, not improved benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds explicit mathematical definitions for previously named classification, caption and motion losses in Equations 14–16, plus segmentation attention. Existing SARA, BiMixCo, diffusion-prior and scheduling mathematics are retained; there are no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same subject-agnostic novelty claim, cognitive-hierarchy and redistribution contributions, approximately 7% average performance tradeoff, and 10-second inference claim. The added analyses support existing claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly explains why image-only pretraining uses SARA to initialize semantics and separate subject tokens despite lacking motion information. Appendix A.6 explains mask rescaling as emphasizing key objects. Main-result interpretations and limitations concerning rare categories and complex scenes remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendices A.5–A.7 substantially expand implementation information: GPT-2 caption decoding, task heads and losses, diffusion conditioning, mask rescaling, linear projection heads and pretrained encoder provenance. v2 also specifies the pretraining objective and RTX 4090 timing hardware, and replaces the future code-release promise with a repository address.

R1.justification: v2 adds related-work citations to Lu et al., Kong et al. and Zhou et al., alongside sources for newly documented implementation dependencies. Appendix A.5 explicitly contrasts NEURONS' shared global representation with VCFLOW's process-specific task features. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include clearer feature notation and classifier explanations, reordered metric descriptions, additional technical and analysis subsections, updated affiliations and publication headers, and acknowledgements. This is localized expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains feature labels and an explicit diffusion-prior label; Tables 5–6 and the four-panel Figure 9 are added. Existing displays retain their content with local relocation and reflow, including Figure 5 and Table 3. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing system substantially easier to understand and reproduce through Appendices A.5–A.7, while the new ablations provide more specific evidence about SARA and HED. The overall gain is limited: the additional quantitative validation concerns subject 1 without uncertainty estimates, and Table 6's non-monotonic effects receive little interpretation. The original benchmark evidence and headline claims remain unchanged.
